correctness.rationale: For 0<a<b,m,T>0, A1=[[a,m],[0,-b-m]] and A2=[[-b-m,0],[m,a]], with A2=P A1 P. Write E=exp(A1 T/2)=[[u,m(u-v)/K],[0,v]], K=a+b+m. The period M=(PE)^2 has Perron multiplier mu_+^2 where mu_+=(q+sqrt(q^2+4uv))/2, and yields Lambda=(a-b-m)/2+(2/T)asinh((m/K)sinh(KT/4)). This is the exact common exponent for nonzero nonnegative initial states. For h=m/K, F(s)=asinh(h sinh s) satisfies F(0)=0 and F''(s)>0, hence F(s)/s strictly increases: Lambda(T downarrow0)=(a-b)/2<0, Lambda(T upward infinity)=a>0. The m derivative is positive by sinh(s)/s>1 and squared numerator comparison, so the unique zero Tc(m) is smooth and decreases. At Tc, (m/K) sinh(KTc/4)=sinh((b+m-a)Tc/4). Expanding the ratio for m downarrow0 gives (m/K)exp(aTc/2)->1. With x=KTc/4 and m upward infinity, the limiting sign is 2ax cosh x-(a+b)sinh x and uniqueness follows monotonicity x coth x; mTc->4x*. Independent direct 2x2 matrix exponential comparisons on 48 parameter tuples matched within 6.6e-14 and give numerical corroboration only, not infinite-parameter proof.
